maria-sales: Heads up — Enterprise prospect (FinReg Co) just returned our SIG + a focused BCP/DR follow-up. They're asking specifically for RTO/RPO targets, backup cadence and retention, cross-region failover flow, and evidence of DR testing. Need a concise thread we can hand to legal + their security intake.
eli-se: Got it. Quick answers first: Hosted API SLA is 99.95% for paid tiers (we'll confirm the public doc link), Dedicated customers can opt into 99.99% contracts. RTO depends on deployment: hosted = seconds-to-minutes (depends on warm capacity + region failover), dedicated = minutes (reserved pools), private = as-configured. RPO: hosted typically <1 minute for active KV/prefix caches persistency; model state isn't persisted across requests (stateless), but customer data (configs, logs) replicated.

sasha-sec: Adding detail for security reviewers: backups for customer metadata/config are encrypted at rest and replicated across two regions. Snapshot cadence: daily full snapshots + hourly incremental for metadata; retention default 30 days, extendable per contract. Backups stored in customer-provisioned buckets for Private, and in managed encrypted storage for Hosted/Dedicated.

ops-oncall: For failover flow — we have active regional routing + automated fallback to secondary region when health checks exceed thresholds. Short flow: primary region health failure -> traffic routed to warm standby region (compatible model variant) -> cache warming + KV reconstruction from latest snapshots -> return to primary after stability window or manual cutback. We run periodic simulated failovers in staging (weekly) and a full runbook DR test for paid customers quarterly.

eli-se: Customer asked for a one-page playbook snippet they can attach to their SIG. Drafting minimal runbook sample below — can you sanity-check?

ops-oncall: Sure.

eli-se: ```
Title: Redwood Hosted - Region Failover (summary)
Trigger: primary region service outage detected by 5m health checks
Steps:
  1) Traffic shift to standby region via smart-routing policy (automated)
  2) Verify model variant compatibility (auto-fallback to quantized variant if needed)
  3) Rehydrate KV cache from latest incremental snapshot
  4) Run smoke tests against critical routes (chat/generate/embeddings)
  5) Observe latency and error budgets for 10min; if >threshold, open incident and escalate to oncall
Recovery: automatic cutback once primary returns healthy and smoke tests pass for 30min
Notes: Data-plane requests are stateless; customer-owned data recovery follows backup retention policy
```

sasha-sec: Looks good. Add encryption and access control bullet: snapshots encrypted with KMS, access logged, retention policy enforced by lifecycle rules. Also note that Private deployments can use customer KMS/HSM and air-gapped backup flows.

maria-sales: Perfect. Can we also list evidence artifacts for their vendor review? They asked for test artifacts.

ops-oncall: We can provide: recent DR playbook, anonymized DR test report (date, scope, outcome), SLA PDF, backup configuration example, and a link to our security architecture doc. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide signed runbook and test evidence under NDA.

eli-se: I'll assemble those into a zip for legal to attach. Quick ask: @sasha-sec — can you confirm the snapshot retention default and whether we have any customers on >365d retention (we need to say yes/no)?

sasha-sec: Default 30d. Yes, a small number of enterprise accounts have custom retention >365d under contract.

maria-sales: Awesome — please drop the doc bundle here when ready. Also @deploy-bot can you share the public SLA link for hosted?

deploy-bot: <https://docs.redwood-inference.com/sla#hosted-uptime> (public SLA page) :white_check_mark:

eli-se: Uploaded draft bundle to the sales drive and linked in thread (private link). Will update with anonymized DR report after redaction.

maria-sales: Thanks team — I'll send to the prospect with the attachments and follow up if they want a walk-through. :thumbsup:
